# Ariada Wiki

> Deterministic public documentation for the Ariada module catalog.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/ariada-org/ariada
Pinned public source commit: 040ee61da6fc63d72bceb28782ac221e9487585c
Catalog schema: https://ariada.org/schemas/public-module-catalog/v1.json

## Catalog

- [Channel matrix](https://ariada.org/channel-matrix.json): 236 modules across 24 packs.
- [Ariada Wiki](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/): localized channel documentation.

## Modules

- [S1: Finish the Shopify app to listing-grade](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s1/) - Planned. The proposed Shopify deliverable would be an app and Shopify App Store listing that merchants can discover, authorize for a development store, and evaluate against their Online Store content before adopting it. Boundary: No installable or listed Shopify app is claimed; a future app would report on storefront pages made available to it, not change themes, publish products, approve checkout behavior, or guarantee that Shopify will accept the listing.
- [S2: Package the VS Code extension for publish](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s2/) - Delivered. The source-delivered VS Code extension provides editor diagnostics and scan commands for developers working in supported web-template files; its distributable object is a VSIX, while Marketplace publication remains separate work. Boundary: The current manifest is private and supports controlled VSIX evaluation rather than a Visual Studio Marketplace or Open VSX listing; diagnostics are advisory, and untrusted workspaces remain read-only.
- [S3: MCP registry packaging for the MCP server](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s3/) - Delivered. The source-delivered MCP server exposes scanning, rule lookup, violation explanation, and fix-suggestion tools to MCP-capable coding hosts; registry metadata would be the discovery object for broader host installation. Boundary: The server exists in source, but no MCP registry or package-registry publication is asserted; hosts decide permissions and tool invocation, and suggestions neither edit code automatically nor certify a result.
- [S4: JetBrains plugin (new build)](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s4/) - Delivered. The source-delivered JetBrains plugin contributes an IDE action and Ariada tool window for developers reviewing the current project file; a signed plugin archive and Marketplace entry would be its distribution surfaces. Boundary: Source delivery supports local archive evaluation but does not establish a JetBrains Marketplace listing; the plugin reports deterministic findings for the selected file and does not rewrite project code or attest to the whole application.
- [S5: Figma plugin (new build)](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s5/) - Planned. A planned Figma plugin would be distributed by manifest during development and, after Figma review, through the Figma Community so product designers and design-system teams could examine selected frames, components, and layer metadata inside a design file. Boundary: No Figma plugin or Community listing is available; a future plugin could analyze only objects exposed by Figma's plugin API and would not silently edit the file, publish a library, validate coded UI, or turn design evidence into compliance certification.
- [S6: CI adapters for non-GitHub CI (new builds)](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s6/) - Planned. The proposed adapters would be reusable pipeline jobs or command wrappers for systems such as CircleCI, Buildkite, and TeamCity, giving CI authors a platform-native way to pass built web artifacts to Ariada and retain reports with a run. Boundary: No non-GitHub adapter is implemented; each future adapter would invoke analysis on declared inputs while the host CI system continues to own runners, secrets, artifact retention, status rules, and release approval.
- [S7: Drupal module](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s7/) - Planned. A proposed Drupal module would be a Drupal.org project and Composer-installable extension used by site builders and editors to review rendered nodes, Views, and theme output from within a Drupal publishing workflow. Boundary: There is no Drupal module release; any future module would surface findings for configured previews or URLs, not edit entities, bypass revisions and moderation, publish content, or claim that a Drupal site is compliant.
- [S8: TYPO3 extension](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s8/) - Planned. The planned TYPO3 extension would be packaged for Composer and the TYPO3 Extension Repository, allowing integrators and backend editors to assess page previews produced by TypoScript, Fluid templates, and content elements. Boundary: No TER or Composer artifact exists; a future extension would read configured rendered previews and return evidence, while TYPO3 continues to control workspaces, permissions, localization, publication, and template changes.
- [S9: Joomla plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s9/) - Planned. A future Joomla extension package and Joomla Extensions Directory entry would let site administrators and template developers review rendered articles, modules, and template overrides before they are exposed on the public site. Boundary: No Joomla install package or directory listing is present; the proposed plugin would report on pages it can render or fetch, without modifying articles, changing menu assignments, publishing modules, or replacing human conformance review.
- [S10: Wix app](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s10/) - Planned. The proposed Wix app would be an App Market product authorized for a Wix site, where site owners and agency designers could request analysis of editor previews or published page URLs during site preparation. Boundary: No Wix app or App Market approval is claimed; a future app could use only Wix-supported APIs and granted site access, and it would not manipulate editor elements, publish the site, alter commerce data, or promise acceptance by Wix.
- [S11: Webflow app](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s11/) - Planned. A planned Webflow App would be installed from the Webflow Marketplace into an authorized workspace or site so designers and agency developers could inspect staging pages, CMS collection templates, and rendered components. Boundary: No Webflow App is implemented or listed; a future app would operate within Webflow's approved Designer and Data API capabilities, not rewrite layouts, publish a site, change CMS records, or certify the resulting production experience.
- [S12: Squarespace extension](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s12/) - Planned. The proposed Squarespace extension would target Squarespace's extension-discovery and site-owner authorization flow, giving merchants or site managers a supported route to submit public or previewable pages for review. Boundary: No Squarespace extension exists, and current extension APIs must be shown to expose the necessary page or preview surface before in-editor analysis can be promised; the concept would not edit blocks, publish pages, or manage commerce operations.
- [S13: Bubble plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s13/) - Planned. A future Bubble plugin would be a Plugin Marketplace asset added to an app in the Bubble editor, where no-code builders could review preview-mode pages and reusable elements before deploying a new version. Boundary: No Bubble plugin is available; a proposed implementation would inspect only preview content and properties exposed to the plugin, not change workflows, database records, privacy rules, deployment versions, or assert production compliance.
- [S14: Sketch plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s14/) - Planned. The planned Sketch plugin would be a signed plugin bundle distributed directly or through Sketch's plugin directory, used by interface designers and library owners to inspect selected artboards, symbols, and overrides. Boundary: No Sketch bundle or directory entry is provided; a future plugin would analyze accessible document objects without changing shared libraries, exporting assets, publishing documents, or treating static artboards as proof of implemented accessibility.
- [S15: ESLint plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s15/) - Planned. A proposed ESLint plugin would be an npm-distributed rule package configured by JavaScript teams in flat or legacy ESLint configuration to flag accessibility-relevant patterns in JSX and other supported syntax during linting. Boundary: No ESLint package or ruleset is published; any future rules would be limited to syntax and semantic information available in the lint AST, not computed styles, browser state, rendered DOM behavior, automatic fixes without safe semantics, or compliance certification.
- [S16: pre-commit / git-hook integration](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s16/) - Planned. The planned integration would be a versioned pre-commit hook repository and hook definition that repository owners add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, giving contributors a local scan of selected staged web files before a commit is created. Boundary: No hook repository or executable entry is available; a future hook would inspect only configured files, leave staging and commit decisions to Git, avoid changing content by default, and never substitute for rendered-page testing.
- [S17: Storybook addon](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s17/) - Delivered. The source-delivered Storybook addon renders Ariada results in an addon panel for component authors and design-system reviewers examining isolated stories; npm publication is a separate distribution step. Boundary: The delivered source covers Storybook preview, manager, decorator, panel, and scan integration but does not prove a registry release; it evaluates the rendered story state, not every application composition or production route.
- [S18: Astro integration](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s18/) - Delivered. The source-delivered Astro integration runs after an Astro build and writes accessibility reports for generated HTML, giving static-site engineers and deployment owners evidence tied to the built site artifact. Boundary: The integration supports Astro 4 or newer build completion from source but has no proven registry release; it sees generated output rather than unpublished editor state, authenticated runtime variants, or every client-side interaction.
- [S19: Vite plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s19/) - Delivered. The source-delivered Vite plugin analyzes HTML served during Vite development and emitted by production builds, placing findings in the workflow used by frontend developers and build-release reviewers. Boundary: The delivered source targets Vite 5 or newer development and build output without establishing npm publication; it does not cover native UI, inaccessible authenticated states that were never rendered, or final compliance judgment.
- [S20: WooCommerce extension](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s20/) - Planned. A planned WooCommerce extension would be a WordPress plugin distributed as a ZIP, through WordPress.org, or through the WooCommerce Marketplace for store operators and ecommerce developers reviewing storefront templates and commerce flows. Boundary: No WooCommerce extension or marketplace listing exists; a future extension would report on configured storefront and test-checkout pages without changing orders, payment settings, products, themes, or the legal accessibility status of the store.
- [S21: Homebrew formula/tap](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s21/) - Planned. The proposed Homebrew distribution would consist of a Ruby formula in a tap, or eventually Homebrew/core, so macOS and Linux command-line users could install a released Ariada executable through `brew`. Boundary: No formula, tap, bottle, or core acceptance is claimed; a formula could only package an independently released executable and checksum, not create scanner functionality, host a service, or establish compliance.
- [S22: Docker image (GHCR + Docker Hub)](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s22/) - Planned. The planned container distribution would publish versioned OCI images to GitHub Container Registry and Docker Hub for CI operators and platform teams that need a reproducible Ariada command environment. Boundary: No image, tag, digest, or registry page is available; a future container would package declared scanner behavior only, while callers remain responsible for mounts, network access, target authorization, secret handling, and interpretation of results.
- [S23: Safari Web Extension](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s23/) - Planned. A future Safari Web Extension would be an extension bundle inside a signed macOS or iOS app distributed through Apple's channels, allowing Safari users to request analysis of the active page from a toolbar or inspector surface. Boundary: No Safari extension, containing app, signing record, or App Store listing exists; a future build would access only user-authorized pages, would not alter the site or bypass browser protections, and would still require Apple's review.
- [S24: Zed editor extension](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s24/) - Planned. The proposed Zed extension would be a registry-discoverable extension manifest and source repository that editor users install to invoke Ariada against workspace files or a configured local target. Boundary: No Zed extension or registry submission is present; implementation would depend on supported Zed extension APIs and could not claim diagnostics, command execution, network access, or automatic edits beyond capabilities actually granted by the editor.
- [S25: Slack app (gate/scan notifications)](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s25/) - Planned. The planned Slack app would be distributed through a Slack app manifest and workspace installation, delivering scan summaries and gate decisions into channels where engineering and accessibility teams already coordinate releases. Boundary: No Slack app, OAuth installation, or App Directory listing exists; a future app would relay explicitly supplied results and actions, not scan Slack conversations, administer channels, operate the underlying CI gate, or certify a release.
- [S26: RapidAPI listing (scan-as-an-API)](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s26/) - Planned. The proposed RapidAPI product would be a hosted API listing with endpoint documentation, plans, quotas, and an interactive console for developers discovering a scan service through the RapidAPI Hub. Boundary: No hosted Ariada API or RapidAPI listing is claimed; a future listing would expose only a separately operated service with documented limits, and neither marketplace presence nor an API response would constitute compliance certification.
- [S27: Sublime Text package](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s27/) - Planned. A planned Sublime Text package would be distributed through Package Control as a versioned repository release, giving web developers commands and result views for files opened in the editor. Boundary: No Package Control entry or Sublime package exists; a future package would delegate to declared Ariada analysis, respect project trust and process settings, avoid changing buffers without consent, and not represent a full browser audit.
- [S28: Neovim/Vim plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s28/) - Planned. The proposed Neovim/Vim plugin would be a versioned Git repository installed by editor plugin managers, exposing commands and quickfix or diagnostic entries to terminal-focused web developers. Boundary: No Vimscript or Lua plugin is delivered; a future integration would require an explicitly configured Ariada executable or service, would not modify buffers by default, and could assess only supplied source or reachable rendered targets.
- [S29: Framer plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s29/) - Planned. A future Framer plugin would be a Marketplace-discovered canvas tool installed into a Framer project, where product designers and site publishers could examine supported layers, components, and previewed pages. Boundary: No Framer plugin or Marketplace entry exists; a future tool would use only objects and previews exposed by Framer, would not rewrite the canvas or publish the website, and could not equate design inspection with production accessibility.
- [S30: Chrome DevTools panel](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s30/) - Planned. The planned DevTools panel would be part of a Chrome extension distributed through the Chrome Web Store, giving frontend debuggers a dedicated surface for analyzing the DOM and state of the currently inspected tab. Boundary: No Chrome extension or Web Store item is available; a future panel would be confined to tabs and host permissions granted by the user, would not edit the originating application, and would remain subject to Chrome extension review and policy.
- [S31: Jenkins plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s31/) - Planned. A proposed Jenkins plugin would be packaged as an HPI or JPI and distributed through an update site, adding a pipeline step and build-action report for Jenkins administrators and release teams. Boundary: No Jenkins plugin or update-center release exists; a future step would analyze configured artifacts or URLs while Jenkins retains control of agents, credentials, approvals, retention, and the final build result.
- [S32: Azure DevOps extension](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s32/) - Planned. The planned Azure DevOps extension would be a VSIX listed in the Visual Studio Marketplace or shared privately to an organization, providing a pipeline task and result surface for Azure project teams. Boundary: No VSIX or Marketplace listing is delivered; a future task would process declared build artifacts or endpoints and publish evidence, without managing service connections, changing branch policies, approving environments, or controlling deployments.
- [S33: Netlify build plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s33/) - Planned. A future Netlify Build Plugin would be an npm package configured for a site and discoverable through Netlify's integrations ecosystem, allowing Jamstack teams to inspect the publish directory during a deploy build. Boundary: No build plugin or Netlify listing exists; the proposed hook would analyze the generated artifact available in its build phase, not alter deploy content, read unrelated environment secrets, cancel production outside configured policy, or certify the live site.
- [S34: Magento / Adobe Commerce module](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s34/) - Planned. The proposed Adobe Commerce module would be a Composer package and possible Commerce Marketplace listing used by merchants and implementation partners to review rendered catalog, content, account, cart, and checkout surfaces on staging. Boundary: No module or Marketplace artifact exists; a future module would report on configured storefront states without changing catalog data, checkout logic, orders, themes, or Adobe Commerce configuration, and would not certify the store.
- [S35: PrestaShop module](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s35/) - Planned. A planned PrestaShop module would be an installable ZIP and Addons Marketplace product for shop managers and theme agencies reviewing category, product, cart, checkout, and account pages. Boundary: No PrestaShop module or Addons listing is available; a future module would analyze selected storefront output while leaving products, orders, customer data, hooks, theme files, and publication under PrestaShop control.
- [S36: winget + Scoop manifests](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s36/) - Planned. The proposed Windows distribution would add a YAML manifest to the Windows Package Manager community repository and JSON manifests to a Scoop bucket so command-line users could install an existing Ariada release. Boundary: No winget or Scoop manifest is present, and manifests cannot precede a stable downloadable executable with verified checksums; they would describe installation only, not add functionality or imply Microsoft, Scoop, or compliance endorsement.
- [S37: Babel plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s37/) - Planned. A future Babel plugin would be an npm-distributed transform-stage package configured by JavaScript build teams to inspect accessibility-relevant JSX or template syntax as Babel traverses source ASTs. Boundary: No Babel plugin is published; any implementation would be static-source analysis unless a separate rendered scan is supplied, would avoid semantics-changing transforms, and could not observe computed layout, browser events, or runtime content.
- [S38: PostCSS plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s38/) - Planned. The planned PostCSS plugin would be an npm package inserted into a CSS processing chain, where stylesheet authors and build engineers could receive findings tied to declarations and selectors visible in the PostCSS AST. Boundary: No PostCSS plugin exists; CSS-only inspection cannot establish text-background contrast, focus behavior, DOM semantics, or cascade outcomes without rendered context, so a future plugin would report only defensible stylesheet evidence and would not rewrite rules silently.
- [S39: esbuild plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s39/) - Planned. A proposed esbuild plugin would be distributed on npm and registered in a build configuration so fast-build users could pass emitted HTML or an explicitly served preview to Ariada after bundling. Boundary: No esbuild plugin package is available; a future plugin would use documented build hooks and declared outputs, not infer accessibility from JavaScript bundles alone, mutate artifacts, or claim coverage of runtime states it never renders.
- [S40: Webpack plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s40/) - Planned. The planned Webpack plugin would be an npm package attached to compiler lifecycle hooks, allowing bundle-platform teams to analyze generated HTML assets or a post-build preview associated with a compilation. Boundary: No Webpack plugin is delivered; an implementation would inspect configured compilation outputs rather than JavaScript chunks as if they were UI, would not rewrite assets, and would leave build failure policy to the consuming configuration.
- [S41: Rollup plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s41/) - Planned. A future Rollup plugin would be an npm-distributed plugin using output-generation hooks to hand relevant HTML artifacts or preview targets to Ariada for site and library demo teams. Boundary: No Rollup plugin exists; because many Rollup builds emit libraries rather than pages, a future integration would require explicit scannable inputs, avoid changing bundles, and make no claim about UI that was not rendered.
- [S42: SWC plugin/wrapper](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s42/) - Planned. The proposed SWC offering would be a supported transform plugin or command wrapper distributed through the appropriate JavaScript or Rust package channel, used by compiler teams to inspect source syntax or explicitly rendered output. Boundary: No SWC plugin or wrapper is implemented, and no universal SWC hook for rendered-page analysis is assumed; source transforms cannot see the final DOM, so any future capability would declare whether it analyzes AST input, build output, or a separate browser target.
- [S43: Turbopack/Next loader integration](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s43/) - Planned. A planned Turbopack-aware Next.js integration would be a versioned package configured through APIs the framework actually supports, giving App Router teams a way to scan rendered development or preview routes rather than treating bundled modules as pages. Boundary: No loader or Turbopack integration exists, and compatibility with Webpack loaders must not be assumed; a future design would depend on documented Next.js and Turbopack extension points and could inspect only routes and states supplied to it.
- [S44: Gulp plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s44/) - Planned. A future Gulp plugin would be an npm package implementing a Vinyl stream transform or reporting step for teams that still assemble web assets through Gulp tasks. Boundary: No Gulp plugin is published; a future stream would analyze matching HTML files or explicit URLs, preserve Vinyl contents unless a documented opt-in says otherwise, and leave task completion and deployment policy to the gulpfile.
- [S45: Grunt plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s45/) - Planned. The proposed Grunt plugin would be an npm-distributed multi-task configured in `Gruntfile` targets, serving teams that need accessibility evidence from HTML generated by older Grunt pipelines. Boundary: No Grunt task package exists; a future task would process declared file globs or preview URLs, would not alter source by default, and could not infer rendered behavior from minified scripts or styles alone.
- [S46: Parcel transformer/reporter](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s46/) - Planned. A planned Parcel package would be configured in `.parcelrc` as a reporter or another justified plugin type, allowing application teams to evaluate built HTML when Parcel completes a development or production bundle. Boundary: No Parcel package is available; the design must use the plugin role that matches Parcel's API and must not disguise analysis as an asset transformation, rewrite bundles, or claim visibility into runtime states absent from the output.
- [S47: Next.js plugin / integration](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s47/) - Planned. The proposed Next.js integration would be an npm package and configuration layer used by framework teams to scan rendered route fixtures or deployment previews across Pages or App Router applications. Boundary: No Next.js package is delivered; a future integration could not derive complete accessibility from `.next` bundles alone and would need explicit URLs, data fixtures, and authentication for dynamic states, without modifying routes or approving deployment.
- [S48: Nuxt module](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s48/) - Planned. A future Nuxt module would be an npm package and Nuxt Modules ecosystem entry added to `nuxt.config`, enabling Nuxt teams to scan prerendered output or explicitly exercised Nitro preview routes. Boundary: No Nuxt module or directory listing exists; a future module would use declared Nuxt hooks, require fixtures for dynamic pages, avoid changing application output, and not claim coverage of client states it did not visit.
- [S49: SvelteKit integration](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s49/) - Planned. The planned SvelteKit integration would be a versioned package configured alongside the framework's Vite and adapter workflow, helping route developers examine prerendered pages and selected SSR previews. Boundary: No SvelteKit integration is implemented; an eventual package would analyze only generated or rendered targets supplied by the project, not infer DOM behavior from compiled components, alter adapter output, or certify authenticated flows.
- [S50: Gatsby plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s50/) - Planned. A proposed Gatsby plugin would be distributed through npm and surfaced in the Gatsby Plugin Library, where site engineers could configure post-build analysis of HTML in the `public` output. Boundary: No Gatsby plugin or library entry exists; a future plugin would scan generated pages and declared previews, not change GraphQL data, page creation, themes, or deployment, and it would not cover client-only states absent from the build.
- [S51: Remix / React-Router integration](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s51/) - Planned. The proposed integration would be a package for Remix or React Router framework-mode applications, used by full-stack teams to exercise rendered routes with representative loader data during preview or test runs. Boundary: No Remix or React Router integration is available; a future package would declare the framework versions and execution mode it supports, require fixtures for data and authentication, and avoid claiming that route modules alone represent rendered accessibility.
- [S52: Angular CLI builder + schematic](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s52/) - Planned. A future Angular package would expose a CLI builder for analysis and a schematic for explicit workspace setup, distributed through npm for Angular architects and enterprise UI teams. Boundary: No builder collection or schematic is published; a future schematic would make reviewable configuration changes only with user consent, while the builder would analyze declared browser output or test URLs rather than claim accessibility from TypeScript compilation.
- [S53: SolidStart integration](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s53/) - Planned. The planned SolidStart integration would be a package connected through supported SolidStart, Vinxi, or Vite configuration so reactive application teams could scan generated pages and selected server-rendered previews. Boundary: No SolidStart package exists; the implementation path must follow stable host hooks rather than assume them, and any future scan would cover only rendered routes and states provided by the project without changing application code.
- [S54: Qwik integration](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s54/) - Planned. A proposed Qwik integration would be an npm package configured with Qwik City and its Vite build, allowing teams to review the accessible result of resumable routes rather than only their serialized bundles. Boundary: No Qwik package is delivered; a future integration would require rendered route states, preserve resumability output, avoid component mutation, and make no claim about lazy interactions or server data that were not exercised.
- [S55: Eleventy (11ty) plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s55/) - Planned. A future Eleventy plugin would be an npm package registered through the Eleventy configuration API, used by static-site authors to scan generated HTML in the output directory after templates and data have resolved. Boundary: No Eleventy plugin is published; a future hook would read generated pages without rewriting content, would leave deployment to the site build, and could not evaluate browser-only interactions absent from static output.
- [S56: Docusaurus plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s56/) - Planned. The planned Docusaurus plugin would be an npm package configured in a docs site and run at a post-build point, helping documentation teams examine generated versioned, localized, and search-enabled pages. Boundary: No Docusaurus plugin exists; an eventual plugin would analyze built or explicitly previewed pages, not author MDX, change sidebars, publish docs, or claim coverage of interactive states that the build did not render.
- [S57: WordPress.org core plugin (general site-scan)](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s57/) - Planned. The proposed general WordPress plugin would be a directory-listed ZIP installed from wp-admin, giving site administrators and plugin reviewers a way to scan configured public or previewable site URLs across themes and content types. Boundary: No WordPress.org plugin or SVN release exists; a future scanner would not modify posts, themes, plugins, users, or publication state, and private previews would require explicit authorized access rather than an assumed crawl.
- [S58: Ghost integration](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s58/) - Planned. A future Ghost integration would be configured through Ghost's integrations surface and APIs, allowing publication teams to submit post previews or rendered site URLs for analysis around the editorial workflow. Boundary: No Ghost integration or marketplace resource exists; a future connection would use only granted Content or Admin API access and reachable previews, would not edit members or posts, publish drafts, change themes, or treat API content as rendered UI.
- [S59: Contentful app](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s59/) - Planned. The planned Contentful App Framework app would be installed into an organization or space and placed in entry, sidebar, or dialog locations so content teams could review a rendered preview tied to an entry. Boundary: No Contentful app or Marketplace listing exists; a future app would access only installed locations and permitted fields, require a project-provided preview endpoint for rendered analysis, and would not change or publish entries.
- [S60: Sanity studio tool/plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s60/) - Planned. A proposed Sanity plugin would be an npm package added to Studio configuration, contributing a document view or tool where editors and Studio developers could analyze the frontend preview for a selected document. Boundary: No Sanity Studio plugin is delivered; a future tool would need a configured preview resolver, would read only authorized document data, and would not patch documents, publish drafts, alter schema, or equate Studio structure with rendered accessibility.
- [S61: Strapi plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s61/) - Planned. A future Strapi plugin would be distributed through npm and the Strapi Marketplace, adding an administration view or entry action for content managers to analyze a frontend preview backed by a Strapi record. Boundary: No Strapi plugin or Marketplace listing exists; a future implementation would require an application-specific preview URL, would respect Strapi roles and permissions, and would not mutate records, publish entries, or scan JSON as though it were UI.
- [S62: Craft CMS plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s62/) - Planned. The planned Craft CMS plugin would be a Composer package and Craft Plugin Store product, providing control-panel actions for editors and project developers to review entry previews rendered through Craft templates. Boundary: No Craft package or Plugin Store entry is available; a future plugin would honor element permissions and preview tokens, would not save or publish entries, change project config, or claim that every frontend state has been tested.
- [S63: Umbraco package (.NET)](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s63/) - Planned. A future Umbraco package would be delivered through NuGet and discoverable in the Umbraco Marketplace, adding a backoffice surface for editors and .NET solution teams to assess rendered content previews. Boundary: No NuGet package or Umbraco listing exists; a future package would operate within backoffice permissions and configured preview routes, without changing content, publishing variants, modifying templates, or certifying the site.
- [S64: Statamic addon](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s64/) - Planned. The proposed Statamic addon would be a Composer-installed Marketplace product integrated with the control panel, allowing Laravel-based site teams to review Live Preview output for entries and collections. Boundary: No Statamic addon or Marketplace listing is delivered; a future addon would inspect configured previews while leaving blueprints, content repositories, revisions, publication, and template edits under Statamic and Git control.
- [S65: Directus extension](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s65/) - Planned. A planned Directus extension would be an extension bundle installed into an instance, contributing an interface, module, panel, or operation chosen to fit the review workflow for collection editors. Boundary: No Directus extension bundle or registry listing exists; a future extension would access only permitted collections and project-defined preview URLs, would not alter items or flows, publish external sites, or interpret API records as rendered pages.
- [S66: Payload CMS plugin](https://wiki.ariada.org/en/modules/s66/) - Planned. A future Payload CMS plugin would be an npm package added to Payload configuration, giving application developers and editorial teams an admin action linked to a draft's rendered preview. A PWA manifest describes install metadata and a service worker controls fetch and caching behavior, while users interact with the linked web application's pages; a proposed audit would combine Ariada page review with limited install-surface checks. Boundary: Neither a valid manifest nor a working service worker proves accessibility. Ariada would not certify offline flows without exercising them, rewrite caching logic, or claim that metadata inspection covers browser and installed-app behavior.

No 1C-Bitrix Marketplace listing or installable archive would be implied.
